examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to choose, use up', paired with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.

Agreed, I will choose a movie.

examples.trans: Now there's a businesswoman, you can see it at once.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Currency unit. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ллар'). Common masculine noun meaning 'dollar' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The ticket costs a hundred dollars.

examples.text: Возьмите! Они десять тысяч долларов стоят!
examples.trans: Take it! It costs ten thousand dollars!

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?

meanings.en: to start working, to come on
meanings.note: Of a machine or device. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start working; to earn', paired with 'зарабатывать'.

Withpair зарабатывать. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'работать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to start working; to earn', paired with 'зарабатывать'.

examples.trans: He earned a lot of money.

examples.text: Не твоё дело! — Это моё дело! — Я их заработала!
examples.trans: None of your business! — It is my business! — I earned it!

meanings.note: In the sky. Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'star; celebrity' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are bright stars in the sky.

examples.text: Вот молодёжь, ничего не знают! Это же Лещенко! Звезда!
examples.trans: Young people these days, they don't know anything! That's Leshchenko! A star!

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.
Каждый день = every day. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('every, each').

examples.text: Аркаш, мне москвичи звонят каждый день. Может, всё-таки передумаем?
examples.trans: Arkasha, the people from Moscow call me every day. Maybe we should reconsider after all?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

examples.text: Специальная комиссия проверяет каждый уголок отеля.

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'of the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это гематома, она и стала причиной потери памяти.
examples.trans: That is a hematoma, it became the cause of memory loss.

examples.text: Андрей, положи её к себе, а то и эту потеряю.
examples.trans: Andrey, put it in your pocket, or I will lose this one too.

examples.text: Я хотел бы просмотреть все документы по закупке продуктов.
examples.trans: I would like to review all the documents on food purchases.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пуск'). Common masculine noun meaning 'vacation, leave' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я в отпуске-то всего два раза был.
examples.trans: I have only been on vacation twice in my whole life.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый отпуск.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new vacation.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ездка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'trip, journey' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тогда эта поездка точно будет удачной.
examples.trans: Then this trip will definitely be successful.

поменять.gloss: to change, to swap, to replace

meanings.en: to change, to switch, to update
meanings.note: to alter or substitute something for a new version

examples.text: Нам нужно срочно поменять наше меню.
examples.trans: We need to urgently change our menu.
What for? We swapped, it's mine.

examples.text: Всё по правилам, как рыцарский турнир.
examples.trans: All by the rules, like a knights' tournament.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'верять'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to check, test, verify', paired with 'проверить'.

examples.trans: You think he is testing us?

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: Простите! = sorry! forgive me!. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

Imperative: прости / простите. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

Простые люди = ordinary people. Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стой'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('simple; ordinary').

рассчитаться.gloss: to settle up / pay the bet

meanings.en: to settle up / pay the bet
meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'считаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to settle up / pay the bet'.

examples.text: Кролик сырой, не рассчитаться ли нам по спору?
examples.trans: The rabbit is raw, shall we settle up on our bet?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и рассчитаться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to settle up on time.

related.gloss: not to to settle up (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'repair shop', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Я лично отвёз её в надёжный сервис.
examples.trans: I personally took it to a reliable repair service.

examples.text: Я просто переживаю за вечерний сервис.
examples.trans: I am simply worried about the evening service.

TV, a film. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мотреть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: special, designed for a particular purpose
meanings.note: From Latin specialis. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пециальный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('special, dedicated, purpose-built').

examples.trans: Calm down, the special operation continues.
A special tool is needed for this.
Everyone down! Special forces at work!

meanings.note: The one over there. Core Russian det meaning 'that' in everyday speech.
in 'то, что ...' = 'what, the thing that'

Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'голок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'corner, nook' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Специальная комиссия проверяет каждый уголок отеля.
examples.trans: A special commission inspects every corner of the hotel.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть уголок.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always corner.

meanings.note: + на: успеть на поезд = catch the train

+ infinitive. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'спеть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make it, to be in time', paired with 'успевать'.

examples.trans: We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: impersonal, + genitive: денег не хватило = there wasn't enough money
Хватит!. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to be enough', paired with 'хватать'.

examples.trans: Gum? I didn't have enough money.

examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: in comparisons: больше, чем = more than

examples.text: А почему нет? Продавец получает больше, чем преподаватель.
